accent.note: Brandable: --accent-base is set from organization branding; #1f3fbf is the default. Dark theme uses color-mix(in oklch, var(--accent-base) 70%, white).

body.purpose: Default text and table cells; --fs-2; prose max 72ch.

label.purpose: Field labels, table headers, nav group headings, state chips; --fs-0, sentence case.

mono.purpose: Evidence excerpts; hashes, refs, paths and section numbers at 0.9em.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Decision bar, popover menus. Dark: 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.4), 0 6px 18px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35).

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Drawer, toasts, off-canvas sidebar. Dark: 0 2px 8px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.45), 0 18px 44px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5).

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: Focused inputs; selected mode card at 20%.

motion.name: control-transition
motion.purpose: Background, border, colour and halo changes on controls.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses all animation and transition durations.

narrative.overview:
REMNANT is the category standard for security and developer tools (left sidebar, tables, detail panels) executed precisely, with one specialised instrument per situation: a transit line for run progress, an RFC-style document header on runs and reports, a chain-of-custody trail on hypotheses and approvals, and line-numbered evidence excerpts. Every surface reads like a page of a well-kept case file: cool neutral paper and ink, quiet rules, numbered sections, references in brackets, hashes beside every claim.

The world is cool neutral paper and ink with a second, cooler panel layer for chrome (sidebar, sign-in side). Density is product-grade and user-switchable (comfortable or compact). Colour is scarce and functional: the brandable accent marks what you can act on, and semantic state colours always arrive paired with a line form, so nothing depends on colour alone. Motion is calm and short; nothing animates for decoration. Light and dark are equal citizens, both shipped and both derived from the same tokens.

Confirmed rejections: the generic SaaS card wall, and hacker-film styling (black screens, neon green, terminal pastiche).
keyCharacteristics: System sans for everything; monospace only for hashes, revisions, references, paths and code.
One brandable accent, reserved for actionable controls; progress and state use the info blue.
State = tone + form: solid (settled), dashed (waiting on a person or queue), pulsing dot (live), struck through (stopped).
1px rules and tonal layers carry structure; shadows are reserved for things that float.
One 12-column grid; panels span 12, 8/4, 6/6 or 4/4/4 and collapse to full width below 1100px.

rules.name: The Actionable Accent Rule
rules.body: The accent appears only on things you can act on (primary buttons, links that do something, focus, the selected choice in a picker). Progress, state and attention counts use Progress Blue (info), never the accent, so an organization's brand colour never reads as a status.

rules.name: The Two-Signal Rule
rules.body: No state is expressed by colour alone. Every status comes from the status vocabulary as a tone plus a form, and the form must be legible in greyscale.

rules.name: The Neutral Translucency Rule
rules.body: Translucent bars and overlays (top bar, decision bar, focus halos, selection, tinted borders) mix in `srgb` against `transparent`, never `oklch`, so they stay neutral instead of drifting in hue. Tinted fills against an opaque surface (state chip ground, alert ground, row hover, danger hover) mix in `oklch`.

rules.name: The Identifier Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks identity, not mood: hashes, revisions, `[H-4]`-style references, file paths, operation names, document numbers and code. Never headings or prose.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Tables, counts, timestamps and the waiting-count numerals use tabular figures.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: If it does not overlap other content, it gets a rule, not a shadow.

dos: Do pick every status look from the status vocabulary (tone + form); use the dashed waiting form for anything waiting on a human.
Do keep the accent on actionable controls and use Progress Blue (`--info`) for progress, live state and attention counts.
Do mix translucent bars and halos in `srgb` against transparent; mix opaque tints in `oklch`.
Do show identifiers (hashes, revisions, refs, paths) in monospace with a copy affordance for hashes.
Do separate structure with 1px rules and the panel layer; keep containers at 6px and controls at 4px.
Do verify both themes and both densities; every colour token has a dark twin.
donts: Don't fill state, progress or counts with the accent; a brand colour must never read as a status.
Don't express a state by colour alone or invent per-page status colours.
Don't add shadows to panels or anything that does not float.
Don't use monospace or uppercase-tracked labels for headings or decoration.
Don't reach for hacker-film styling: black-and-neon screens, terminal pastiche, decorative animation.
